title: How to Call Any Country: Calling Codes Guide
h1: How to call any country: international calling codes explained
description: Learn how to call any country: dial your exit code, then the country calling code, then the number. Find every country's code in our free directory.
faq: How do I call another country?

Dial your country's international exit code (often 00, or + on a mobile), then the destination's country calling code, then the local phone number. For example, to call the United Kingdom you dial your exit code, then 44, then the number without its leading 0. Our country calling code directory lists the code and dialing steps for every country.
What is a country calling code?

It is the number you dial after the exit code to reach a specific country, such as +1 for the United States and Canada, +44 for the United Kingdom, +91 for India or +971 for the United Arab Emirates. Each country has its own code; some, like +1, are shared across many countries.
Where can I look up a country code?

Use the free Insight Dial calling code directory. It has a page for every country (for example India) showing the code, an example number, how to dial it and the current local time, plus a page for each numeric code such as +44.
body:
Calling abroad trips people up because the format changes from country to country. The good news is that the pattern is always the same three parts. Get those right and you can call anywhere.

The three parts of an international call

  1. Your exit code — the number that tells your phone network you are dialing out of the country. It is often 00, and on any mobile you can simply press + instead.
  2. The country calling code — which country you are calling, such as 1 for the US and Canada, 44 for the UK, 91 for India or 971 for the UAE.
  3. The local number — the phone number itself. In most countries you drop the leading 0 (the national trunk prefix) when dialing from abroad.

So a UK number written locally as 020 7946 0000 is dialed from abroad as +44 20 7946 0000 — exit code or +, then 44, then the number without the leading 0.

Look up any country code

You do not have to memorise them. Insight Dial has a free country calling code directory with a page for every country and every code. Each country page — for example United Kingdom or India — shows the calling code, an example number, how to dial it and the current local time there, so you can also avoid calling in the middle of someone's night.

If you run a business on phone calls

For a business taking or buying calls across countries, the country code is only the start. You also want to know where a caller is, route them to the right team, and keep a record of every call. That is what Insight Dial does: it tracks where each call comes from, routes it by country and region, and turns it into searchable data — so international call flow is something you can measure, not guess at. You can also try the free tools or browse US and Canada area codes.
